sources.text:
Trump says one officer shot at DC press dinner, suspect in custody
Editor's note: This page summarizes news of the shooting at the White House Correspondents' dinner for Saturday, April 25. For the latest on the shooting at the dinner, visit USA TODAY's coverage for Sunday, April 26.
A suspect is in custody after a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner that caused law enforcement to swiftly evacuate President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump and other guests from the high-profile event.
"Everyone owes a tremendous debt of gratitude to the courage of law enforcement," Trump told reporters during a news briefing, after authorities rushed him and other top officials to the White House.
Police believe the suspect charged a security checkpoint at the hotel where the dinner was scheduled and exchanged gunfire with officers. The suspect is 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen, of Torrance, California, according to multiple media reports, which cited anonymous law enforcement sources.
FBI Director Kash Patel told reporters agents quickly subdued the alleged shooter, though he did not name the man, and a long gun and shell casings were found on the scene. He will be arraigned on at least two charges on Monday, U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro said.
The president told reporters that the suspect in the incident shot one Secret Service agent at close range, but he was saved by a bulletproof vest. Trump said he spoke to the officer, who was in "high spirits," and told the man "we love him and respect him."
The incident reminded many that former President Ronald Reagan was injured in an assassination attempt at the same hotel in March 1981. Then-White House Press Secretary James Brady and several law enforcement officials were also wounded.
Traditional afterparties move forward
Karissa Waddick
Some of the many afterparties planned around the White House Correspondents' Dinner moved forward Saturday night – despite the shooting and shutdown of the main event.
TIME Magazine opted to still host its bash at the Swiss Ambassador's Residence, telling guests in an email that it wanted to recognize "the importance of the vital role journalists play everyday and especially at times like this." MSNOW also continued with its"Democracy After Hours" party inside a former trolley car station.
The White House Correspondents' Dinner is known for spawning extravagant parties with celebrity attendees throughout the weekend in Washington. It's unclear how many are expected to go on as scheduled.
Suspect was a guest at Washington Hilton hotel
Karissa Waddick
Investigators believe the suspect was a guest at the Washington Hilton hotel where the dinner was taking place, Interim DC Police Chief Jeffery Carroll confirmed during a news conference. He said police have "secured" his room and are in the process of determining what is inside.
How was shooting suspect able to get a weapon inside hotel?
Francesca Chambers
To enter the ballroom of the Washington Hilton during the annual White House Correspondents' Association dinner, guests were required to present a dinner ticket and pass through magnetometers.
But in order to access the lobby of the hotel, they needed only to show their dinner ticket or an invitation to a pre-dinner party taking place on site. They were not swept for firearms.
Hotel guests also had access to the surrounding area. That the alleged shooter was able to brandish a weapon in the first place will raise questions about how security is handled at large gatherings that are attended by the president and members of the Cabinet in the future.
Melania Trump attends White House briefing
Swapna Venugopal Ramaswamy
First lady Melania Trump stood silently as President Donald Trump addressed the press in the White House briefing room on Saturday.
"The first lady's team is in good spirits and appreciative of law enforcement for their quick and effective reaction," said Nick Clemens, spokesperson for the first lady, who along with the president was rushed from the White House correspondents’ dinner after shots were fired.
Trump: 'I'm not a basket case'
Maureen Groppe
President Donald Trump said he’s not rattled by the violence that occurred at the White House Correspondents' Dinner and leads "a pretty normal life considering it’s a dangerous life."
“I think I handle it as well as it can be handled,” he told reporters afterwards. “I’m not a basket case. I really take it as it is. I do it for the country.”
Suspect facing 2 charges, US attorney says
Karissa Waddick
Jeanine Pirro, U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, said the suspect in custody is being charged with two counts, including using a firearm during a crime of violence and assault on a federal officer using a dangerous weapon.
The suspect will be arraigned on Monday, Pirro said.
"It is clear, based upon what we know so far, that this individual was intent on doing as much harm and as much damage as he could," Pirro said.
Trump: No job is 'more dangerous'
Maureen Groppe
President Donald Trump, who’s been the target of multiple assassination attempts, said being president is a riskier job than race car driving or bull riding.
“I can't imagine that there’s any profession that's more dangerous,” he said.
Asked why he thinks people are going after him, Trump said would-be assassins target “the most impactful people.”
“I hate to say I’m honored by that, but I’ve done a lot,” Trump said. “We’re going to do great things, but with that comes risk.”
Law enforcement IDs suspect
Karissa Waddick
Law enforcement officials have identified the suspect as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen, of Torrance, California, according to reports from the New York Times, the Associated Press and CBS News citing anonymous law enforcement officials.
Suspect under observation at local hospital
Karissa Waddick
Washington, DC Mayor Muriel Bowser said the shooting suspect has been transported to the hospital and is being evaluated. The suspect was not shot, said Jeffery Carroll, the interim DC police chief.
A Secret Service agent was also transported to the hospital. The agent "took a round" to his bullet proof vest, the police chief said.
Bowser said the suspect in custody is believed to have been the lone gunman.
Senate leader credits first responders with averting 'night of horror'
Sen. James Lankford, R-Oklahoma, credited first responders for preventing "night of horror and tragedy" at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.
"Cindy and I join many others in prayers of gratitude for the safety of President Trump and everyone else at the White House Correspondents Dinner tonight. A night of horror and tragedy was prevented by brave first responders. We’ll learn more in the days ahead but for now let’s be grateful that no lives were lost and everyone is safe," Lankford said in a post on X.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-New York, also expressed appreciation for the work of law enforcement at the event.
"I am closely monitoring the unfolding situation at the White House Correspondents Dinner. I’m grateful for the quick response of law enforcement and am praying everyone remains safe," Schumer wrote on X.
Trump: 'I thought it was a tray'
Maureen Groppe
President Donald Trump’s first thought when he heard a loud sound during the dinner was that one of the many waitstaff in the packed ballroom had dropped a serving tray.
“I heard a noise and sort of thought it was a tray. I thought it was a tray going down. I’ve heard that many times,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “And it was pretty loud noise. And it was from quite far away.”
“It was either a tray or a bullet," the president said. "I was hoping it was a tray, but it wasn’t.”
The president said he and the first lady were immediately whisked away.
“It was very quick,” he said. “There wasn’t a lot of time to be thinking because it was a matter of seconds before we were out the door.”
Melania Trump said ‘it’s a bad noise,’ President Trump said
Rebecca Morin
President Donald Trump said first lady Melania Trump, who was also in attendance at the dinner, said there was a “bad noise” after three consecutive pops rang out from the ballroom.
Trump said he heard a noise, which he thought was a tray.
“Melania said ‘it's a bad noise,'” Trump said during a press conference in the White House press briefing room.
Wolf Blitzer witnessed shooting
Karissa Waddick
CNN anchor Wolf Blitzer was feet away from the gunman when he fired outside of the ballroom at the Washington Hilton hotel.
"It was loud. It was scary," Blitzer told USA TODAY of the moment. "The cops got on top of him. And then they got on top of me to protect me. And then they took me away into a secure room, the men's room."
Trump says experience was 'traumatic' for first lady
Francesca Chambers
Trump said at his news conference that the shooting was a "rather traumatic experience" for first lady Melania Trump, who was on the dais at the White House Correspondents' dinner at the time of the shooting.
The president again said the dinner would be rescheduled. "We're not going to cancel things out, because we can't do that. We wanted to stay tonight," Trump told reporters. "I fought like hell to stay, but it was protocol."
He indicated that Secret Service was unsure if the shooter acted lone.
Trump said this is why ‘we need the ballroom’
Rebecca Morin
After a gunman rushed security at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, President Donald Trump said this is why “we need the ballroom” on the White House grounds.
Trump said the Washington Hilton, which was hosting the dinner, is “not a particularly secure building.”
“I didn't want to say this, but this is why we have to have all of the attributes of what we're planning at the White House,” Trump said, noting it would be “a larger room” that would be bulletproof. “We need the ballroom. That's why Secret Service, that's why the military are demanding it.”
Suspect had long gun, FBI chief says
Sarah D. Wire
FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed that the alleged shooter used a long gun.
"The evidence response unit is examining all the ballistics that were found on scene to include the long gun and the shell casings," he told reporters in the White House briefing room.
Trump, officials give details on suspect
Karissa Waddick
Acting U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the investigation is ongoing and officials are working to get search warrants.
"I promise you justice will be served," Blanche said.
FBI Director Kash Patel said agents quickly subdued the suspect. He confirmed the suspect used a long gun. "We are conducting witness interviews," Patel said.
Trump told reporters the suspect was from California.
Man with 'multiple weapons' charged security, Trump says
Karissa Waddick
Speaking at the White House, Trump said a man "with multiple weapons" charged a security checkpoint at the Washington Hilton hotel and was taken down by Secret Service officers. He posted a video of the man on social media.
Trump said one officer was shot but was wearing a bulletproof vest.
"I just spoke to the officer and he's in great shape," Trump said of the agent.
Kerry Kennedy: 'It was terrifying'
Maureen Groppe
Kerry Kennedy, the daughter of slain Sen. Robert F. Kennedy, said she hit the floor after hearing a loud bang of gun shots and shouts to “Get down, get down, get down!”
One of her tablemates, Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Maryland, “heroically protected me, whispering, 'You’re ok, you’re ok, you’re ok,’” Kennedy said on social media.
Scores of Secret Service agents rushed into the room, searching for Cabinet secretaries to pull them to safety, she recounted.
“Then security started yelling, '`'Go, go, go,’ demanding that we leave,” Kennedy wrote. “It was terrifying.”
Witness says she saw suspect bust through security checkpoint
A guest at the dinner and Air Force veteran Erin Thielman says she witnessed the suspected shooter running and busting through the security checkpoint at the hotel.
She had walked out of the dinner to call her teenage son who was babysitting his younger siblings.
“As soon as he picked up I heard three loud gunshots and then quickly saw the man flat on his face,” Thielman told USA TODAY. “He was carrying a rifle and appeared to be wearing a rope of magazines like a crossbody bag.”
Thielman said she then ran back to the dinner and remembered yelling “gun, shooter, gun shooter” and alerting security to close the ballroom’s doors.
Dana White calls chaos 'F------ awesome'
Karissa Waddick and Ralphie Aversa
Dana White, a close friend of President Donald Trump's and the CEO of Ultimate Fighting Championship, called the chaos that unfolded after gunshots were heard outside the White House Correspondents' Dinner "f------ awesome."
"I literally took every minute of it in. And, it was a pretty crazy unique experience," White told USA TODAY shortly after the events unfolded. He said he saw tables being flipped over and officials with guns running into the ballroom and screaming at attendees to take cover.
"I didn't get down," White said. "We were sitting right in front of the table, right in front of where the president was. Nobody got tackled, but guys came in looking for shooters. And they came toward our table," White added. "I thought the shooter was over by us or something."
House leaders react to shooting at WHCA dinner
Republican Speaker Mike Johnson, who attended the dinner Saturday night alongside his wife, said he was "praying for our country tonight" in a post to social media.
"Kelly and I were at the event tonight, and we’re thankful no innocent people were harmed and everyone is now safe. We’re grateful as always for the law enforcement and first responders who acted so quickly to bring the situation under control. Praying for our country tonight," Johnson wrote in an X post.
Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, thanked law enforcement for quickly intervening in a post on X.
"Thankful for the swift law enforcement action to protect everyone from gunfire at the White House Correspondents Dinner. Praying for the safety of those who may remain in harm’s way. The violence and chaos in America must end," Jeffries wrote.
At least one person in custody, FBI and Secret Service confirm
Aysha Bagchi
The FBI and Secret Service both confirmed at least one person is in custody in relation to the shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner.
The FBI's Washington Field Office said in a post on X that a "subject" is in custody, and that the office's National Capital Response Squad has responded to the shooting.
Secret Service spokesperson Anthony Guglielmi said in a post on X that one "individual" is in custody.
'It was very scary,' congressman says
Maureen Groppe
Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Indiana, one of the members of Congress who attended the dinner, said he had been talking with his table mates from NewsNation about how much freedom there is in the United States when he heard gunshots.
“It was very scary,” he said in a video posted on social media. “We all just jumped underneath the table. The stuff on the table was falling over. Drinks spilled over. It was all over my arm,” he said.
Stutzman and the other members of Congress were evacuated along with members of the Cabinet.
Trump to speak at White House, says first lady and Cabinet members are safe
Sarah D. Wire
President Donald Trump said on social media he will speak from the White House briefing room at about 10:10 p.m. ET
"Law Enforcement has requested that we leave the premises, consistent with protocol, which we will do, immediately. I will be giving a press conference in 30 minutes from the White House Press Briefing Room. The First Lady, plus the Vice President, and all Cabinet members, are in perfect condition," he said on Truth Social.
Dinner to be rescheduled in next month
Karissa Waddick
The White House Correspondents' Dinner will not continue this evening and will be rescheduled in the next 30 days, White House Correspondents' Association President Weijia Jiang said while speaking inside the Washington Hilton ballroom.
She said the president wanted the dinner to continue, but law enforcement requested the area be vacated. She said President Donald Trump pushed for the dinner to be rescheduled.
The president will host a press conference shortly.
USA TODAY reporter gives update from inside Correspondents' Dinner
Ralphie Aversa
Secret Service says all protectees safe
Aysha Bagchi
All protectees of the Secret Service, which include the president and first lady, are safe, Secret Service spokesperson Anthony Guglielmi confirmed in a post on X.
One individual is in custody, and the Secret Service is investigating the incident, which took place near the main magnetometer screening area at the dinner, Guglielmi said.
"The condition of those involved is not yet known, and law enforcement is actively assessing the situation," he said.
'The subject is now offsite,' WHCA official reports
Bart Jansen
Fox News Senior White House reporter Jacqui Heinrich said on social media that she and others who were at the head table were told by President Trump's detail that someone tried to get through the magnetometer with a gun.
“The counter assault team did their job (unclear what that means) and the subject is now offsite,” said Heinrich, treasurer of the White House Correspondents Association.
Reporters who travel with president leaving building
Bart Jansen
The pool of reporters who travel with the president were loaded into vans at 9:28 p.m. ET, suggesting the president was leaving the building.
“We are departing the Hilton,” the reporters said.
“The whole motorcade is still here but we have no information on where POTUS is,” the reporters said, in reference to the president of the United States. “Your pooler has asked and has not received any updates.”
Hegseth's security surrounded him after loud noise: Brennan
Bart Jansen
Margaret Brennan, the CBS anchor of “Face the Nation,” said she was at a table near Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, whose security surrounded him after the loud noise.
“We got under table,” Brennan said on social media. “Secretary Hegseth was at nearby table. His security surrounded him. I asked what is going on. He said unclear. Shortly after the cabinet was pulled.”
Secret Service said 'shots fired' and announced an arrest, reporters at scene say
Bart Jansen
Reporters traveling with President Trump said they heard several loud bangs and were rushed from the room by Secret Service agents with guns drawn.
“Shots fired,” Secret Service agents said, according to an email at 8:39 p.m from reporters who are part of the press pool that normally accompanies the president to events.
The Secret Service said by 8:44 p.m. the shooter was in custody, according to the reporters.
The pool had not left the building by 8:56 p.m., which suggested the president was still there.
The pool is being ushered back into the ballroom, reporters said at 9:16 p.m. But the reporters had no information about the president’s whereabouts.
Trump says alleged shooter apprehended
Sarah D. Wire
President Donald Trump said in a social media post that an alleged shooter has been apprehended.
"Quite an evening in D.C. Secret Service and Law Enforcement did a fantastic job. They acted quickly and bravely. The shooter has been apprehended, and I have recommended that we “LET THE SHOW GO ON” but, will entirely be guided by Law Enforcement. They will make a decision shortly. Regardless of that decision, the evening will be much different than planned, and we’ll just, plain, have to do it again," Trump wrote on Truth Social.
What does security look like getting into the dinner?
Rebecca Morin
Before people could even enter the Washington Hilton hotel for the White House Correspondents' Dinner, security asked for invitations to events at the hotel.
Several outlets hosted pre-receptions ahead of the dinner.
To get down to the dinner itself, attendees need a physical tickets. Attendees pass through a magnetometer and purses or bags were checked.
CNN's Wolf Blitzer: 'Shooting randomly'
Sarah D. Wire
CNN's Wolf Blitzer reported on air that he was near one gunman "who was shooting just randomly."
"I was a few feet away from this one gunman who was shooting just randomly," he said. Blitzer said he heard at least six shots before the gunman stopped firing. He said he saw the alleged gunman laying on the ground.
Ballroom smells of gunpowder, attendees say
Sarah D. Wire
A strong smell of gunfire hung in the air as a chaotic scene unfolded in the basement ballroom of the Washington Hilton Hotel where the White House Correspondents Association's annual dinner is taking place, according to reporters in the room.
Muffled bangs were heard by guests. Chairs littered the ballroom as reporters and guests ducked for cover. Secret Service rushed in from the main entrance.
Speaker Mike Johnson, a Louisiana Republican who was a guest of USA TODAY, was in the bathroom at the time. His wife Kelly was seated with reporters and editors at USA TODAY when the incident occurred and was safe under the table.
After the apparent threat was said to be cleared, maroon cloth napkins were seen scattered across the floor like confetti, according to USA TODAY reporters in the room.
WHCA president says dinner to resume
Karissa Waddick
Members of the press were being evacuated from the dinner when White House Correspondents' Association President Weijia Jiang walked onto stage and announced that the program would resume shortly.
"Please just be patient as we figure out just how much time it will be but it shouldn't be that much longer," she said.
What happened at White House Correspondents Dinner? Loud bangs heard.
Karissa Waddick
President Trump speaking with CBS News reporter Weijia Jiang and others seated on a raised platform when a series of loud bangs erupted. Clattering could be heard in the background of a live video feed of the event.
Trump and others did not appear to hear the sounds. They continued talking for about a minute before they were swept off stage by security. People in the audience could be heard yelling "stay down." Security officials with guns straddled the table where Trump sat and pointed guns toward the audience, as other armed officers ran back and forth on the stage.
After about 15 minutes, members of the press and other attendees inside the ballroom began leaving the hotel.
See the moment Trump was rushed out of White House Correspondents' Dinner
Armed officers enter Washington Hilton
Karissa Waddick
Armed officers ran through the halls of the Washington Hilton hotel after loud bangs were heard near the ballroom. Members of the press remained inside after President Trump and other dignitaries were escorted out of the dinner.
Trump evacuated, attendees take cover
Karissa Waddick
USA TODAY reporters inside the ballroom said they hear what sounded like gunshots. Reporters heard "USA" chants near the ballroom.
Attendees, including President Donald Trump, took cover as security officers came to the main table. Trump and other people seated at the head table were evacuated from the room.
Trump, Melania, Vance enter
Karissa Waddick
President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump and Vice President JD Vance walked onto the stage with other dignitaries at the start of the White House Correspondents' Dinner.
The president is wearing a black tuxedo and Melania Trump is in an all black jumpsuit.
DC’s political power players arrive
Rebecca Morin
By 8 p.m. ET, many of the more than 200 tables were packed with the press and some of Washington’s top political power players.
House Speaker Mike Johnson was spotted, alongside his wife. FBI Director Kash Patel was also in attendance. Sen. John Fetterman was walking into the dinner shortly after 8:10 p.m. and as the WHCA members were being introduced.
What’s on the menu?
Rebecca Morin
It’s a three-course menu fit for Mar-a-Lago.
For the first course: spring peas decorated around a piece of buffalo burrata, and lemon-scented cucumbers sprinkled on a salad.
The second course will be an upscale surf and turf, consisting of prime Chateaubriand – a center-cut beef tenderloin –and Maine lobster. For the sides, whipped potato gratin, tri-color roasted cauliflower, sherry-braised carrots and pickled shallots.
And for dessert, a grand opera cake, which the program describes as having espresso cream, almond sponge and buttercream chocolate ganache.
An orchestra and a photo line
Rebecca Morin
The first thing that greets you inside the International Ballroom at the Washington Hilton? A map of more than 250 tables.
Reporters, editors and guests of the many publications in attendance filed in, searching for their tables, yapping with old – or possibly new – friends and lining up to get a photo in front of the main table. Behind the table was an orchestra, barely playing loud enough to hear.
The wall behind the lectern in front of the main table says, “White House Correspondents’ Association. Celebrating The First Amendment.”
On the tables, a pin that says “America 250,” a theme of the dinner and one of the reasons why President Donald Trump said he would be in attendance.
Trump’s viral moment at the 2011 White House Correspondents' Dinner
Rebecca Morin
It was the moment that changed Trump’s political trajectory. At least, that’s what political insiders say.
Trump attended the White House Correspondents' Dinner in April 2011 as a guest of the Washington Post. At the time, the then-business mogul had repeatedly criticized President Barack Obama and promoted a conspiracy theory that Obama was not born in the United States.
At the dinner that year, Trump was the butt of many jokes – including from the president himself.
“Donald Trump is here tonight,” Obama said during his speech. “I know that he’s taken some flak lately, but no one is happier, no one is prouder to put this birth certificate matter to rest than The Donald. And that's because he can finally get back to focusing on the issues that matter. Like did we fake the moon landing?”
Trump kept a straight face during Obama’s speech, and at one point even waved during the president’s remarks. Comedian Seth Meyers, who was the host that year, also joked about Trump and his White House ambitions.
“Donald Trump has been saying he will run for president as a Republican – which is surprising, since I just assumed he was running as a joke,” Meyers said.
In an interview with “Fox & Friends” the next morning, Trump said: “I didn’t know that I’d be virtually the sole focus, and I guess when you’re leading in most of the polls, that tends to happen.”
‘Shame!’: Protesters outside correspondents’ dinner venue
Rebecca Morin
At least two dozen protesters stood across from the Washington Hilton, chanting “shame” and holding anti-war signs.
The demonstrators also waved Iran and Palestine flags as the rain came down and dinner attendees walked into the hotel.
One homemade sign said “Lady Liberty Does Not Bend To Tyrants.” Other signs said “No War for Israel” and “No War for Iran.”
Correspondents' Dinner weather report: Chilly and wet
Rebecca Morin
Let’s hope that this evening's April shower will bring May flowers.
It’s a brisk 57 degrees here in DC, but really it feels chillier than that. (Especially for someone who is from deep South Texas!)
A steady stream of rain is coming down, but let’s hope that doesn’t put a damper on Saturday’s dinner.
Nicki Minaj to attend White House Correspondents’ Dinner
Mary Walrath-Holdridge
Rapper Nicki Minaj's high-profile friendship with President Donald Trump has snagged her a seat at tonight's White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner.
Minaj will attend as a guest of Fox News, which is also throwing its own VIP party before Saturday's official dinner, Fox confirmed to USA TODAY. The cocktail pre-party at the Washington Hilton will be occupied by other high-profile figures alongside Minaj, including Turning Point USA’s Erika Kirk and NASA astronaut Butch Wilmore, Fox confirmed.
Minaj has stirred controversy among fans with her support of the president, most recently after speaking at a Treasury event in January to endorse "Trump Accounts." In December, she sat down with Kirk – a prominent conservative figure and the widow of Charlie Kirk – at a Turning Point USA event, where she praised both Trump and Vice President JD Vance for their "relatability."
Oz Pearlman to host White House Correspondents' dinner
Anthony Robledo
Mentalist Oz Pearlman is hosting the annual White House Correspondents' Dinner, breaking with the tradition of comedians like Seth Meyers and Trevor Noah headlining the event.
Comedian Amber Ruffin hosted last year's dinner.
Weijia Jiang, president of the White House Correspondents' Association, said in a statement that the renowned performing artist will offer a thrilling glimpse into the minds of newsmakers. "We look forward to an exciting, fresh, and interactive evening as we celebrate the First Amendment and Washington news coverage together," Jiang said.
How to watch the White House Correspondents’ Dinner
Rebecca Morin
It’s one of Washington’s biggest parties of the year.
The White House Correspondents’ Dinner, hosted at the Washington Hilton hotel, will be attended by President Donald Trump for the first time as president. Trump did not attend the dinner during his first term and skipped out last year for the first dinner of his second term.
USA TODAY will be livestreaming the event starting at 6 p.m. ET.
Journalists urge protest of Trump at correspondents' dinner
Kathryn Palmer
More than 200 journalists, journalism organizations and press freedom groups called for the White House Correspondents’ Association to use the dinner to defend press freedom amid ongoing threats to the First Amendment – many that they say have been spearheaded by Trump and his administration.
While some attendees have pledged to wear pins on their gowns and lapels in subtle protest, the group of journalists in an open letter urged the association to go a step further and directly condemn the president for dozens of actions they say are intended to undermine the nation's press freedoms.
"We, the undersigned, call upon the White House Correspondents' Association to use the occasion of the White House Correspondents' Dinner to forcefully demonstrate opposition to President Trump’s efforts to trample freedom of the press," the April 20 letter said.
When did Trump last attend White House Correspondents' Dinner?
Rebecca Morin
Trump last went to the dinner in 2015, where his appearance was more subdued than in previous years.
His most notable appearance was back in 2011. Trump was roasted by comedian Seth Meyers and President Barack Obama, who made fun of the “Apprentice” host’s White House ambitions and pushed back at a debunked conspiracy theory that Trump had promoted at the time about Obama having not been born in the United States.
During Trump’s 2015 appearance at the dinner, Obama, who was president at the time, only referenced Trump once.
“And Donald Trump is here. Still,” Obama said at the 2015 dinner.
Trump has not previously attended the dinner as president. Every president since the inception of the annual dinner has attended it at least once during their term since Calvin Coolidge in 1924.
What is the White House Correspondents' Dinner?
Rebecca Morin
The White House Correspondents Association, a nonprofit member organization of journalists who cover the presidency, hosts an annual dinner each year that brings together members of the press, lawmakers and celebrities.
Dubbed “nerd prom,” the dinner raises funds to support the White House Correspondents' Association's First Amendment scholarships and programs to promote its work.
The first dinner was hosted at the Arlington Hotel that was located near McPherson Square in Washington, DC, on May 7, 1921, according to the association.

sources.news_title: Trump says one officer shot at DC dinner, suspect in custody: Live updates
sources.text:
Trump says one officer shot at DC press dinner, suspect in custody
Editor's note: This page summarizes news of the shooting at the White House Correspondents' dinner for Saturday, April 25. For the latest on the shooting at the dinner, visit USA TODAY's coverage for Sunday, April 26.
A suspect is in custody after a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner that caused law enforcement to swiftly evacuate President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump and other guests from the high-profile event.
"Everyone owes a tremendous debt of gratitude to the courage of law enforcement," Trump told reporters during a news briefing, after authorities rushed him and other top officials to the White House.
Police believe the suspect charged a security checkpoint at the hotel where the dinner was scheduled and exchanged gunfire with officers. The suspect is 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen, of Torrance, California, according to multiple media reports, which cited anonymous law enforcement sources.
FBI Director Kash Patel told reporters agents quickly subdued the alleged shooter, though he did not name the man, and a long gun and shell casings were found on the scene. He will be arraigned on at least two charges on Monday, U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro said.
The president told reporters that the suspect in the incident shot one Secret Service agent at close range, but he was saved by a bulletproof vest. Trump said he spoke to the officer, who was in "high spirits," and told the man "we love him and respect him."
The incident reminded many that former President Ronald Reagan was injured in an assassination attempt at the same hotel in March 1981. Then-White House Press Secretary James Brady and several law enforcement officials were also wounded.
Traditional afterparties move forward
Karissa Waddick
Some of the many afterparties planned around the White House Correspondents' Dinner moved forward Saturday night – despite the shooting and shutdown of the main event.
TIME Magazine opted to still host its bash at the Swiss Ambassador's Residence, telling guests in an email that it wanted to recognize "the importance of the vital role journalists play everyday and especially at times like this." MSNOW also continued with its"Democracy After Hours" party inside a former trolley car station.
The White House Correspondents' Dinner is known for spawning extravagant parties with celebrity attendees throughout the weekend in Washington. It's unclear how many are expected to go on as scheduled.
Suspect was a guest at Washington Hilton hotel
Karissa Waddick
Investigators believe the suspect was a guest at the Washington Hilton hotel where the dinner was taking place, Interim DC Police Chief Jeffery Carroll confirmed during a news conference. He said police have "secured" his room and are in the process of determining what is inside.
How was shooting suspect able to get a weapon inside hotel?
Francesca Chambers
To enter the ballroom of the Washington Hilton during the annual White House Correspondents' Association dinner, guests were required to present a dinner ticket and pass through magnetometers.
But in order to access the lobby of the hotel, they needed only to show their dinner ticket or an invitation to a pre-dinner party taking place on site. They were not swept for firearms.
Hotel guests also had access to the surrounding area. That the alleged shooter was able to brandish a weapon in the first place will raise questions about how security is handled at large gatherings that are attended by the president and members of the Cabinet in the future.
Melania Trump attends White House briefing
Swapna Venugopal Ramaswamy
First lady Melania Trump stood silently as President Donald Trump addressed the press in the White House briefing room on Saturday.
"The first lady's team is in good spirits and appreciative of law enforcement for their quick and effective reaction," said Nick Clemens, spokesperson for the first lady, who along with the president was rushed from the White House correspondents’ dinner after shots were fired.
Trump: 'I'm not a basket case'
Maureen Groppe
President Donald Trump said he’s not rattled by the violence that occurred at the White House Correspondents' Dinner and leads "a pretty normal life considering it’s a dangerous life."
“I think I handle it as well as it can be handled,” he told reporters afterwards. “I’m not a basket case. I really take it as it is. I do it for the country.”
Suspect facing 2 charges, US attorney says
Karissa Waddick
Jeanine Pirro, U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, said the suspect in custody is being charged with two counts, including using a firearm during a crime of violence and assault on a federal officer using a dangerous weapon.
The suspect will be arraigned on Monday, Pirro said.
"It is clear, based upon what we know so far, that this individual was intent on doing as much harm and as much damage as he could," Pirro said.
Trump: No job is 'more dangerous'
Maureen Groppe
President Donald Trump, who’s been the target of multiple assassination attempts, said being president is a riskier job than race car driving or bull riding.
“I can't imagine that there’s any profession that's more dangerous,” he said.
Asked why he thinks people are going after him, Trump said would-be assassins target “the most impactful people.”
“I hate to say I’m honored by that, but I’ve done a lot,” Trump said. “We’re going to do great things, but with that comes risk.”
Law enforcement IDs suspect
Karissa Waddick
Law enforcement officials have identified the suspect as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen, of Torrance, California, according to reports from the New York Times, the Associated Press and CBS News citing anonymous law enforcement officials.
Suspect under observation at local hospital
Karissa Waddick
Washington, DC Mayor Muriel Bowser said the shooting suspect has been transported to the hospital and is being evaluated. The suspect was not shot, said Jeffery Carroll, the interim DC police chief.
A Secret Service agent was also transported to the hospital. The agent "took a round" to his bullet proof vest, the police chief said.
Bowser said the suspect in custody is believed to have been the lone gunman.
Senate leader credits first responders with averting 'night of horror'
Sen. James Lankford, R-Oklahoma, credited first responders for preventing "night of horror and tragedy" at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.
"Cindy and I join many others in prayers of gratitude for the safety of President Trump and everyone else at the White House Correspondents Dinner tonight. A night of horror and tragedy was prevented by brave first responders. We’ll learn more in the days ahead but for now let’s be grateful that no lives were lost and everyone is safe," Lankford said in a post on X.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-New York, also expressed appreciation for the work of law enforcement at the event.
"I am closely monitoring the unfolding situation at the White House Correspondents Dinner. I’m grateful for the quick response of law enforcement and am praying everyone remains safe," Schumer wrote on X.
Trump: 'I thought it was a tray'
Maureen Groppe
President Donald Trump’s first thought when he heard a loud sound during the dinner was that one of the many waitstaff in the packed ballroom had dropped a serving tray.
“I heard a noise and sort of thought it was a tray. I thought it was a tray going down. I’ve heard that many times,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “And it was pretty loud noise. And it was from quite far away.”
“It was either a tray or a bullet," the president said. "I was hoping it was a tray, but it wasn’t.”
The president said he and the first lady were immediately whisked away.
“It was very quick,” he said. “There wasn’t a lot of time to be thinking because it was a matter of seconds before we were out the door.”
Melania Trump said ‘it’s a bad noise,’ President Trump said
Rebecca Morin
President Donald Trump said first lady Melania Trump, who was also in attendance at the dinner, said there was a “bad noise” after three consecutive pops rang out from the ballroom.
Trump said he heard a noise, which he thought was a tray.
“Melania said ‘it's a bad noise,'” Trump said during a press conference in the White House press briefing room.
Wolf Blitzer witnessed shooting
Karissa Waddick
CNN anchor Wolf Blitzer was feet away from the gunman when he fired outside of the ballroom at the Washington Hilton hotel.
"It was loud. It was scary," Blitzer told USA TODAY of the moment. "The cops got on top of him. And then they got on top of me to protect me. And then they took me away into a secure room, the men's room."
Trump says experience was 'traumatic' for first lady
Francesca Chambers
Trump said at his news conference that the shooting was a "rather traumatic experience" for first lady Melania Trump, who was on the dais at the White House Correspondents' dinner at the time of the shooting.
The president again said the dinner would be rescheduled. "We're not going to cancel things out, because we can't do that. We wanted to stay tonight," Trump told reporters. "I fought like hell to stay, but it was protocol."
He indicated that Secret Service was unsure if the shooter acted lone.
Trump said this is why ‘we need the ballroom’
Rebecca Morin
After a gunman rushed security at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, President Donald Trump said this is why “we need the ballroom” on the White House grounds.
Trump said the Washington Hilton, which was hosting the dinner, is “not a particularly secure building.”
“I didn't want to say this, but this is why we have to have all of the attributes of what we're planning at the White House,” Trump said, noting it would be “a larger room” that would be bulletproof. “We need the ballroom. That's why Secret Service, that's why the military are demanding it.”
Suspect had long gun, FBI chief says
Sarah D. Wire
FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed that the alleged shooter used a long gun.
"The evidence response unit is examining all the ballistics that were found on scene to include the long gun and the shell casings," he told reporters in the White House briefing room.
Trump, officials give details on suspect
Karissa Waddick
Acting U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the investigation is ongoing and officials are working to get search warrants.
"I promise you justice will be served," Blanche said.
FBI Director Kash Patel said agents quickly subdued the suspect. He confirmed the suspect used a long gun. "We are conducting witness interviews," Patel said.
Trump told reporters the suspect was from California.
Man with 'multiple weapons' charged security, Trump says
Karissa Waddick
Speaking at the White House, Trump said a man "with multiple weapons" charged a security checkpoint at the Washington Hilton hotel and was taken down by Secret Service officers. He posted a video of the man on social media.
Trump said one officer was shot but was wearing a bulletproof vest.
"I just spoke to the officer and he's in great shape," Trump said of the agent.
Kerry Kennedy: 'It was terrifying'
Maureen Groppe
Kerry Kennedy, the daughter of slain Sen. Robert F. Kennedy, said she hit the floor after hearing a loud bang of gun shots and shouts to “Get down, get down, get down!”
One of her tablemates, Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Maryland, “heroically protected me, whispering, 'You’re ok, you’re ok, you’re ok,’” Kennedy said on social media.
Scores of Secret Service agents rushed into the room, searching for Cabinet secretaries to pull them to safety, she recounted.
“Then security started yelling, '`'Go, go, go,’ demanding that we leave,” Kennedy wrote. “It was terrifying.”
Witness says she saw suspect bust through security checkpoint
A guest at the dinner and Air Force veteran Erin Thielman says she witnessed the suspected shooter running and busting through the security checkpoint at the hotel.
She had walked out of the dinner to call her teenage son who was babysitting his younger siblings.
“As soon as he picked up I heard three loud gunshots and then quickly saw the man flat on his face,” Thielman told USA TODAY. “He was carrying a rifle and appeared to be wearing a rope of magazines like a crossbody bag.”
Thielman said she then ran back to the dinner and remembered yelling “gun, shooter, gun shooter” and alerting security to close the ballroom’s doors.
Dana White calls chaos 'F------ awesome'
Karissa Waddick and Ralphie Aversa
Dana White, a close friend of President Donald Trump's and the CEO of Ultimate Fighting Championship, called the chaos that unfolded after gunshots were heard outside the White House Correspondents' Dinner "f------ awesome."
"I literally took every minute of it in. And, it was a pretty crazy unique experience," White told USA TODAY shortly after the events unfolded. He said he saw tables being flipped over and officials with guns running into the ballroom and screaming at attendees to take cover.
"I didn't get down," White said. "We were sitting right in front of the table, right in front of where the president was. Nobody got tackled, but guys came in looking for shooters. And they came toward our table," White added. "I thought the shooter was over by us or something."
House leaders react to shooting at WHCA dinner
Republican Speaker Mike Johnson, who attended the dinner Saturday night alongside his wife, said he was "praying for our country tonight" in a post to social media.
"Kelly and I were at the event tonight, and we’re thankful no innocent people were harmed and everyone is now safe. We’re grateful as always for the law enforcement and first responders who acted so quickly to bring the situation under control. Praying for our country tonight," Johnson wrote in an X post.
Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, thanked law enforcement for quickly intervening in a post on X.
"Thankful for the swift law enforcement action to protect everyone from gunfire at the White House Correspondents Dinner. Praying for the safety of those who may remain in harm’s way. The violence and chaos in America must end," Jeffries wrote.
At least one person in custody, FBI and Secret Service confirm
Aysha Bagchi
The FBI and Secret Service both confirmed at least one person is in custody in relation to the shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner.
The FBI's Washington Field Office said in a post on X that a "subject" is in custody, and that the office's National Capital Response Squad has responded to the shooting.
Secret Service spokesperson Anthony Guglielmi said in a post on X that one "individual" is in custody.
'It was very scary,' congressman says
Maureen Groppe
Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Indiana, one of the members of Congress who attended the dinner, said he had been talking with his table mates from NewsNation about how much freedom there is in the United States when he heard gunshots.
“It was very scary,” he said in a video posted on social media. “We all just jumped underneath the table. The stuff on the table was falling over. Drinks spilled over. It was all over my arm,” he said.
Stutzman and the other members of Congress were evacuated along with members of the Cabinet.
Trump to speak at White House, says first lady and Cabinet members are safe
Sarah D. Wire
President Donald Trump said on social media he will speak from the White House briefing room at about 10:10 p.m. ET
"Law Enforcement has requested that we leave the premises, consistent with protocol, which we will do, immediately. I will be giving a press conference in 30 minutes from the White House Press Briefing Room. The First Lady, plus the Vice President, and all Cabinet members, are in perfect condition," he said on Truth Social.
Dinner to be rescheduled in next month
Karissa Waddick
The White House Correspondents' Dinner will not continue this evening and will be rescheduled in the next 30 days, White House Correspondents' Association President Weijia Jiang said while speaking inside the Washington Hilton ballroom.
She said the president wanted the dinner to continue, but law enforcement requested the area be vacated. She said President Donald Trump pushed for the dinner to be rescheduled.
The president will host a press conference shortly.
USA TODAY reporter gives update from inside Correspondents' Dinner
Ralphie Aversa
Secret Service says all protectees safe
Aysha Bagchi
All protectees of the Secret Service, which include the president and first lady, are safe, Secret Service spokesperson Anthony Guglielmi confirmed in a post on X.
One individual is in custody, and the Secret Service is investigating the incident, which took place near the main magnetometer screening area at the dinner, Guglielmi said.
"The condition of those involved is not yet known, and law enforcement is actively assessing the situation," he said.
'The subject is now offsite,' WHCA official reports
Bart Jansen
Fox News Senior White House reporter Jacqui Heinrich said on social media that she and others who were at the head table were told by President Trump's detail that someone tried to get through the magnetometer with a gun.
“The counter assault team did their job (unclear what that means) and the subject is now offsite,” said Heinrich, treasurer of the White House Correspondents Association.
Reporters who travel with president leaving building
Bart Jansen
The pool of reporters who travel with the president were loaded into vans at 9:28 p.m. ET, suggesting the president was leaving the building.
“We are departing the Hilton,” the reporters said.
“The whole motorcade is still here but we have no information on where POTUS is,” the reporters said, in reference to the president of the United States. “Your pooler has asked and has not received any updates.”
Hegseth's security surrounded him after loud noise: Brennan
Bart Jansen
Margaret Brennan, the CBS anchor of “Face the Nation,” said she was at a table near Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, whose security surrounded him after the loud noise.
“We got under table,” Brennan said on social media. “Secretary Hegseth was at nearby table. His security surrounded him. I asked what is going on. He said unclear. Shortly after the cabinet was pulled.”
Secret Service said 'shots fired' and announced an arrest, reporters at scene say
Bart Jansen
Reporters traveling with President Trump said they heard several loud bangs and were rushed from the room by Secret Service agents with guns drawn.
“Shots fired,” Secret Service agents said, according to an email at 8:39 p.m from reporters who are part of the press pool that normally accompanies the president to events.
The Secret Service said by 8:44 p.m. the shooter was in custody, according to the reporters.
The pool had not left the building by 8:56 p.m., which suggested the president was still there.
The pool is being ushered back into the ballroom, reporters said at 9:16 p.m. But the reporters had no information about the president’s whereabouts.
Contributing: White House pool report
Trump says alleged shooter apprehended
Sarah D. Wire
President Donald Trump said in a social media post that an alleged shooter has been apprehended.
"Quite an evening in D.C. Secret Service and Law Enforcement did a fantastic job. They acted quickly and bravely. The shooter has been apprehended, and I have recommended that we “LET THE SHOW GO ON” but, will entirely be guided by Law Enforcement. They will make a decision shortly. Regardless of that decision, the evening will be much different than planned, and we’ll just, plain, have to do it again," Trump wrote on Truth Social.
What does security look like getting into the dinner?
Rebecca Morin
Before people could even enter the Washington Hilton hotel for the White House Correspondents' Dinner, security asked for invitations to events at the hotel.
Several outlets hosted pre-receptions ahead of the dinner.
To get down to the dinner itself, attendees need a physical tickets. Attendees pass through a magnetometer and purses or bags were checked.
CNN's Wolf Blitzer: 'Shooting randomly'
Sarah D. Wire
CNN's Wolf Blitzer reported on air that he was near one gunman "who was shooting just randomly."
"I was a few feet away from this one gunman who was shooting just randomly," he said. Blitzer said he heard at least six shots before the gunman stopped firing. He said he saw the alleged gunman laying on the ground.
Ballroom smells of gunpowder, attendees say
Sarah D. Wire
A strong smell of gunfire hung in the air as a chaotic scene unfolded in the basement ballroom of the Washington Hilton Hotel where the White House Correspondents Association's annual dinner is taking place, according to reporters in the room.
Muffled bangs were heard by guests. Chairs littered the ballroom as reporters and guests ducked for cover. Secret Service rushed in from the main entrance.
Speaker Mike Johnson, a Louisiana Republican who was a guest of USA TODAY, was in the bathroom at the time. His wife Kelly was seated with reporters and editors at USA TODAY when the incident occurred and was safe under the table.
After the apparent threat was said to be cleared, maroon cloth napkins were seen scattered across the floor like confetti, according to USA TODAY reporters in the room.
WHCA president says dinner to resume
Karissa Waddick
Members of the press were being evacuated from the dinner when White House Correspondents' Association President Weijia Jiang walked onto stage and announced that the program would resume shortly.
"Please just be patient as we figure out just how much time it will be but it shouldn't be that much longer," she said.
What happened at White House Correspondents Dinner? Loud bangs heard.
Karissa Waddick
President Trump speaking with CBS News reporter Weijia Jiang and others seated on a raised platform when a series of loud bangs erupted. Clattering could be heard in the background of a live video feed of the event.
Trump and others did not appear to hear the sounds. They continued talking for about a minute before they were swept off stage by security. People in the audience could be heard yelling "stay down." Security officials with guns straddled the table where Trump sat and pointed guns toward the audience, as other armed officers ran back and forth on the stage.
After about 15 minutes, members of the press and other attendees inside the ballroom began leaving the hotel.
See the moment Trump was rushed out of White House Correspondents' Dinner
Armed officers enter Washington Hilton
Karissa Waddick
Armed officers ran through the halls of the Washington Hilton hotel after loud bangs were heard near the ballroom. Members of the press remained inside after President Trump and other dignitaries were escorted out of the dinner.
Trump evacuated, attendees take cover
Karissa Waddick
USA TODAY reporters inside the ballroom said they hear what sounded like gunshots. Reporters heard "USA" chants near the ballroom.
Attendees, including President Donald Trump, took cover as security officers came to the main table. Trump and other people seated at the head table were evacuated from the room.
Trump, Melania, Vance enter
Karissa Waddick
President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump and Vice President JD Vance walked onto the stage with other dignitaries at the start of the White House Correspondents' Dinner.
The president is wearing a black tuxedo and Melania Trump is in an all black jumpsuit.
DC’s political power players arrive
Rebecca Morin
By 8 p.m. ET, many of the more than 200 tables were packed with the press and some of Washington’s top political power players.
House Speaker Mike Johnson was spotted, alongside his wife. FBI Director Kash Patel was also in attendance. Sen. John Fetterman was walking into the dinner shortly after 8:10 p.m. and as the WHCA members were being introduced.
What’s on the menu?
Rebecca Morin
It’s a three-course menu fit for Mar-a-Lago.
For the first course: spring peas decorated around a piece of buffalo burrata, and lemon-scented cucumbers sprinkled on a salad.
The second course will be an upscale surf and turf, consisting of prime Chateaubriand – a center-cut beef tenderloin –and Maine lobster. For the sides, whipped potato gratin, tri-color roasted cauliflower, sherry-braised carrots and pickled shallots.
And for dessert, a grand opera cake, which the program describes as having espresso cream, almond sponge and buttercream chocolate ganache.
An orchestra and a photo line
Rebecca Morin
The first thing that greets you inside the International Ballroom at the Washington Hilton? A map of more than 250 tables.
Reporters, editors and guests of the many publications in attendance filed in, searching for their tables, yapping with old – or possibly new – friends and lining up to get a photo in front of the main table. Behind the table was an orchestra, barely playing loud enough to hear.
The wall behind the lectern in front of the main table says, “White House Correspondents’ Association. Celebrating The First Amendment.”
On the tables, a pin that says “America 250,” a theme of the dinner and one of the reasons why President Donald Trump said he would be in attendance.
Trump’s viral moment at the 2011 White House Correspondents' Dinner
Rebecca Morin
It was the moment that changed Trump’s political trajectory. At least, that’s what political insiders say.
Trump attended the White House Correspondents' Dinner in April 2011 as a guest of the Washington Post. At the time, the then-business mogul had repeatedly criticized President Barack Obama and promoted a conspiracy theory that Obama was not born in the United States.
At the dinner that year, Trump was the butt of many jokes – including from the president himself.
“Donald Trump is here tonight,” Obama said during his speech. “I know that he’s taken some flak lately, but no one is happier, no one is prouder to put this birth certificate matter to rest than The Donald. And that's because he can finally get back to focusing on the issues that matter. Like did we fake the moon landing?”
Trump kept a straight face during Obama’s speech, and at one point even waved during the president’s remarks. Comedian Seth Meyers, who was the host that year, also joked about Trump and his White House ambitions.
“Donald Trump has been saying he will run for president as a Republican – which is surprising, since I just assumed he was running as a joke,” Meyers said.
In an interview with “Fox & Friends” the next morning, Trump said: “I didn’t know that I’d be virtually the sole focus, and I guess when you’re leading in most of the polls, that tends to happen.”
‘Shame!’: Protesters outside correspondents’ dinner venue
Rebecca Morin
At least two dozen protesters stood across from the Washington Hilton, chanting “shame” and holding anti-war signs.
The demonstrators also waved Iran and Palestine flags as the rain came down and dinner attendees walked into the hotel.
One homemade sign said “Lady Liberty Does Not Bend To Tyrants.” Other signs said “No War for Israel” and “No War for Iran.”
Correspondents' Dinner weather report: Chilly and wet
Rebecca Morin
Let’s hope that this evening's April shower will bring May flowers.
It’s a brisk 57 degrees here in DC, but really it feels chillier than that. (Especially for someone who is from deep South Texas!)
A steady stream of rain is coming down, but let’s hope that doesn’t put a damper on Saturday’s dinner.
Nicki Minaj to attend White House Correspondents’ Dinner
Mary Walrath-Holdridge
Rapper Nicki Minaj's high-profile friendship with President Donald Trump has snagged her a seat at tonight's White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner.
Minaj will attend as a guest of Fox News, which is also throwing its own VIP party before Saturday's official dinner, Fox confirmed to USA TODAY. The cocktail pre-party at the Washington Hilton will be occupied by other high-profile figures alongside Minaj, including Turning Point USA’s Erika Kirk and NASA astronaut Butch Wilmore, Fox confirmed.
Minaj has stirred controversy among fans with her support of the president, most recently after speaking at a Treasury event in January to endorse "Trump Accounts." In December, she sat down with Kirk – a prominent conservative figure and the widow of Charlie Kirk – at a Turning Point USA event, where she praised both Trump and Vice President JD Vance for their "relatability."
Oz Pearlman to host White House Correspondents' dinner
Anthony Robledo
Mentalist Oz Pearlman is hosting the annual White House Correspondents' Dinner, breaking with the tradition of comedians like Seth Meyers and Trevor Noah headlining the event.
Comedian Amber Ruffin hosted last year's dinner.
Weijia Jiang, president of the White House Correspondents' Association, said in a statement that the renowned performing artist will offer a thrilling glimpse into the minds of newsmakers. "We look forward to an exciting, fresh, and interactive evening as we celebrate the First Amendment and Washington news coverage together," Jiang said.
How to watch the White House Correspondents’ Dinner
Rebecca Morin
It’s one of Washington’s biggest parties of the year.
The White House Correspondents’ Dinner, hosted at the Washington Hilton hotel, will be attended by President Donald Trump for the first time as president. Trump did not attend the dinner during his first term and skipped out last year for the first dinner of his second term.
USA TODAY will be livestreaming the event starting at 6 p.m. ET.
Journalists urge protest of Trump at correspondents' dinner
Kathryn Palmer
More than 200 journalists, journalism organizations and press freedom groups called for the White House Correspondents’ Association to use the dinner to defend press freedom amid ongoing threats to the First Amendment – many that they say have been spearheaded by Trump and his administration.
While some attendees have pledged to wear pins on their gowns and lapels in subtle protest, the group of journalists in an open letter urged the association to go a step further and directly condemn the president for dozens of actions they say are intended to undermine the nation's press freedoms.
"We, the undersigned, call upon the White House Correspondents' Association to use the occasion of the White House Correspondents' Dinner to forcefully demonstrate opposition to President Trump’s efforts to trample freedom of the press," the April 20 letter said.
When did Trump last attend White House Correspondents' Dinner?
Rebecca Morin
Trump last went to the dinner in 2015, where his appearance was more subdued than in previous years.
His most notable appearance was back in 2011. Trump was roasted by comedian Seth Meyers and President Barack Obama, who made fun of the “Apprentice” host’s White House ambitions and pushed back at a debunked conspiracy theory that Trump had promoted at the time about Obama having not been born in the United States.
During Trump’s 2015 appearance at the dinner, Obama, who was president at the time, only referenced Trump once.
“And Donald Trump is here. Still,” Obama said at the 2015 dinner.
Trump has not previously attended the dinner as president. Every president since the inception of the annual dinner has attended it at least once during their term since Calvin Coolidge in 1924.
What is the White House Correspondents' Dinner?
Rebecca Morin
The White House Correspondents Association, a nonprofit member organization of journalists who cover the presidency, hosts an annual dinner each year that brings together members of the press, lawmakers and celebrities.
Dubbed “nerd prom,” the dinner raises funds to support the White House Correspondents' Association's First Amendment scholarships and programs to promote its work.
The first dinner was hosted at the Arlington Hotel that was located near McPherson Square in Washington, DC, on May 7, 1921, according to the association.

sources.news_title: Trump to headline 2026 White House Correspondents' Dinner for the first time as president
sources.text:
President Trump is attending the White House Correspondents’ Dinner Saturday for the first time as commander in chief after boycotting the annual event last year and each year during his first term.
The dinner will take place Saturday, April 25, at the Washington Hilton.
"The White House Correspondents Association has asked me, very nicely, to be the Honoree at this year’s Dinner, a long and storied tradition since it began in 1924, under then President Calvin Coolidge," Trump posted on his Truth Social last month, adding that it would be his "Honor to accept their invitation."
The White House Correspondents’ Association’s president, Weijia Jiang, said the organization was "happy" with the president’s decision to attend.
"For more than 100 years, the journalists of the White House Correspondents’ Association have enjoyed an evening with the president," Jiang said in a statement last month. "We’re happy the president has accepted our invitation and look forward to hosting him."
DAN RATHER AMONG 200 JOURNALISTS DEMANDING TRUMP BE CALLED OUT AT WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS' DINNER
The president had skipped the event in years past, saying that decision was due to the press being "extraordinarily bad" to him.
Despite the annual invitation and Trump’s acceptance, hundreds of journalists are going after the president, having signed an open letter urging the White House Correspondents’ Association to call out the president and "forcefully demonstrate opposition" to his "efforts to trample freedom of the press."
"The dinner has long served as a symbol of the vital and irreplaceable role of a free press in American democracy and a celebration of the First Amendment and the journalists who uphold it," he open letter states.
"President Trump's systematic, sustained, and unprecedented attacks on the free press... render his presence at such an event a profound contradiction of its purpose.
"The collective weight of the administration’s actions — retaliatory access bans, coercive regulatory investigations, frivolous lawsuits against the press, defunding of public broadcasting, dismantling of international broadcasting, physical restrictions on journalists, personal verbal attacks on reporters, assaults on the media in official White House press releases and social media posts, the arrest of journalists, and the pardoning of those who committed violence against the press — represent the most systematic and comprehensive assault on freedom of the press by a sitting American president."
Notable signatories on the letter are former CBS News anchor Dan Rather, former ABC News White House correspondent Sam Donaldson, former NBC News anchor Ann Curry and PBS NewsHour correspondent Stephanie Sy.
A spokesperson for the White House simply pointed to Trump's Truth Social post announcing he was attending the dinner when previously asked about the open letter.
CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS
Trump did attend the event as a private citizen in 2011 during the Obama administration. President Barack Obama made a joke about Trump during that event saying, "Say what you will about Mr. Trump. He certainly would bring some change to the White House. Let’s see what we’ve got up there."
Obama then featured an image of the White House with a neon sign that said "Trump White House Hotel Casino Golf Course" with gold columns and a chandelier.
During his second term, Trump has actually taken to remodeling the White House with a new ballroom under construction and his addition of gold molding to the Oval Office.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP
Fox News' Joseph Wulfsohn contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: Trump to attend White House Correspondents’ Dinner for 1st time as president to ‘make it the GREATEST, HOTTEST and MOST SPECTACULAR’
sources.text:
OAN Staff Katherine Mosack
1:55 PM – Saturday, April 25, 2026
President Donald Trump is set to attend the White House Correspondents’ Dinner for the first time as commander-in-chief after boycotting the event each year he was in office thus far.
The president will headline the dinner on Saturday evening at 7:00 p.m. ET at the Washington Hilton in Washington, D.C. Attendees usually include White House correspondents and journalists from major news organizations, senior administration officials, lawmakers and other media executives.
Trump is to deliver remarks alongside this year’s host, mentalist Oz Pearlman, who is best known for his appearances on “America’s Got Talent.” The selection of Pearlman, a magician whose claim to fame is a unique ability to read minds, as a host differs from the tradition of choosing a stand-up comedian.
“The White House Correspondents Association has asked me, very nicely, to be the Honoree at this year’s Dinner, a long and storied tradition since it began in 1924, under then President Calvin Coolidge,” Trump posted on Truth Social last month, adding that it would be his “Honor to accept their invitation.”
“In honor of our Nation’s 250th Birthday, and the fact that these ‘Correspondents’ now admit that I am truly one of the Greatest Presidents in the History of our Country, the G.O.A.T., according to many, it will be my Honor to accept their invitation, and work to make it the GREATEST, HOTTEST, and MOST SPECTACULAR DINNER, OF ANY KIND, EVER!”
“Because the Press was extraordinarily bad to me, FAKE NEWS ALL, right from the beginning of my First Term, I boycotted the event, and never went as Honoree,” he explained. “However, I look forward to being with everyone this year. Hopefully, it will be something very Special.”
The last appearance Trump made at the annual dinner was in 2015, not long before announcing his bid for the presidency.
Ahead of his remarks, Trump’s daughter-in-law, Lara Trump, told Fox News host Charlie Hurt, “Get your popcorn ready.”
“This is going to be a time like we’ve never seen,” she said. “Everybody goes back, of course, whenever President Trump, as a citizen, went to the White House Correspondents’ Dinner and President Obama at the time told jokes about him, and they say, ‘Oh, that’s the reason Donald Trump decided to run for president.’ I would push back on that claim. There are a lot of reasons Donald Trump wanted to run for president.”
Trump also attended the dinner in 2011, before the 2012 presidential election. At the time, former President Barack Obama called him out by name for questioning if Obama was born within the United States — a requirement for running for president. In light of the release of his long-form birth certificate from Hawaii in an effort to put the issue to rest, Obama jokingly played what he claimed to be his birth video, which turned out to be a few clips from the opening number of “The Lion King.”
In a rare moment between a president and a private citizen, Obama dedicated several minutes to roasting Trump, including questioning his credentials and temperament. Viewers jokingly looked back on this moment as the “origin story” for Trump’s presidency.
Lara continued, “It’s such a full-circle moment because most of the folks who are in attendance at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner … are no fans of Donald Trump, but they actually desperately need Donald Trump. They love every second of Donald Trump because he gives them ratings unlike anyone else possibly can. He gives them continual information to talk about.”
“He has been preparing to go into this snake pit of the White House Correspondents’ Dinner his entire life,” she said. “He’s gonna have jokes, he’s one of the funniest people I have ever met. And I will tell you that if they don’t leave there absolutely in love with Donald Trump, I’ll be shocked.”
She added on the “Citizen McCain with Meghan McCain” podcast, “I think everyone should get ready ‘cause he’s going to do some roasting and we know that he doesn’t hold anything back.”
